automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.policy: Include only public items with direct visible publication or update evidence strictly within the last two days. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, snippet-only, header-only, and boundary-only dates.

searched_topics: agent and tool security, including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

routing_context.summary: Broad AI companies, models, products, frameworks, MCP servers, and general development practices are upstream-owned. This artifact keeps only security-specific facts, affected boundaries, exploit or mitigation context, and routing notes for ai-security-wiki.

search_methods: Read automation memory before collection and checked the prior processed collector artifact for overlap.
Read docs/wiki/federation.md and the local, ai-wiki, and ai-dev-wiki topic indexes for ownership boundaries.
Queried NVD CVE API for strict-window terms including mcp, llm, agent, prompt, and model.
Fetched direct CVE JSON from cveawg.mitre.org for qualifying CVEs.
Checked public OpenAI pages and Deployment Safety Hub content for direct September 3 safety and cyber-defense updates.
Searched local raw, raw/processed, and docs/wiki for selected CVE identifiers and entity names before classifying items as fresh.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra with Critical cybersecurity capability and new deployment safeguards

visible_dates.date_basis: Visible page date on OpenAI safety overview

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra is its first broadly deployed model to reach the Preparedness Framework Critical cybersecurity capability threshold. The safety overview states the model can, with tools and access, find previously unknown flaws and develop new exploit paths across protected systems, and describes stricter internal isolation, checkpoint encryption, trajectory monitoring, blocking alignment evaluations, external deployment misalignment monitoring, improved prompt-injection robustness, and residual monitorability concerns.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary model safety and deployment-control disclosure
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: GPT-6 Astra external deployment; Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under OpenAI Preparedness Framework
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a security capability threshold change for a frontier model, with concrete release-gate, monitoring, prompt-injection, browsing/workplace-action, and model-misuse controls that affect AI security risk management.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Broad OpenAI and GPT-6 Astra model coverage belongs in ai-wiki; ai-security-wiki should keep the Critical cyber capability threshold, safeguards, monitorability limits, and deployment-gate implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from primary OpenAI pages with visible September 3, 2026 date; deeper system-card metrics should be rechecked during ingest if quoted.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI commits $1B Daybreak access and support for frontline cyber defenders

visible_dates.date_basis: Visible page date on OpenAI security post

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: OpenAI announced Daybreak for Frontline Defenders, committing $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access, training, technical support, and partnerships for essential-service defenders. The post names U.S. water and wastewater systems, electric grid operators, state and local governments, community and regional banks, nonprofits, and open-source maintainers, and says Daybreak access can help review legacy code, analyze suspicious activity, identify and validate vulnerabilities, prioritize risks, and develop and test fixes.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary mitigation and cyber-defense access-control program announcement
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Daybreak, Daybreak Blue, Daybreak Red, Daybreak for America, Daybreak Defense Network, MS-ISAC pilot
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The item is a concrete mitigation and assurance workflow change for AI-enabled cyber defense, including authorized access, training, technical assistance, remediation support, and partner delivery into defender workflows.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: General OpenAI product and partner ecosystem details belong in ai-wiki; ai-security-wiki owns the governed cyber-defense access, remediation, essential-services, and release-gate implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from primary OpenAI source with visible September 3, 2026 date.

qualifying_findings.title: n8n Workflow Tool node can exfiltrate credentials through inline sub-workflow references
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-85166 describes n8n failing to validate credential references in inline workflow JSON for nodes that execute inline sub-workflows, including the Workflow Tool node. A shared-workflow editor or API user can persist a node referencing a credential they do not own; later execution under an identity that does hold the credential can resolve and send the secret to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE vulnerability record with vendor advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: n8n before 2.35.4 and 2.36.x before 2.36.2; NVD CVSS 7.2 HIGH; CWE-863
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: n8n is an agent/workflow automation surface where model-triggered tool execution can cross credential ownership boundaries, making least privilege and workflow review critical.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Broad n8n workflow-product coverage belongs upstream; ai-security-wiki should keep the credential exfiltration, inline sub-workflow, delegated identity, and fixed-version facts.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct NVD and CVE timestamps plus GitHub advisory reference; ingest should reconcile the two version trains.

qualifying_findings.title: Ollama tensor-layer model pulls can be redirected to internal hosts
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-85180 describes Ollama failing to validate redirect destinations when pulling tensor-layer models. An unauthenticated attacker who controls a registry can serve a malicious tensor-layer manifest and cause the server to issue GET requests to arbitrary destinations, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE vulnerability record with public issue and advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Ollama 0.30.0 through 0.33.2; NVD CVSS 7.5 HIGH; CWE-918
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model artifact acquisition becomes a network egress and cloud-metadata SSRF boundary, connecting model supply chain trust to runtime infrastructure exposure.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: General Ollama product and model-runtime coverage belongs in ai-wiki; ai-security-wiki owns the model-pull SSRF, registry trust, metadata endpoint, and fixed-boundary implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from direct NVD and CVE timestamps; GitHub issue predates the window and is included only as technical reference, not as date qualification.

qualifying_findings.title: Agentimus AI SEO and MCP WordPress plugin has subscriber broken access control
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-84779 reports broken access control for the Agentimus - AI SEO, llms.txt & MCP for AI Agents WordPress plugin. The CVE marks versions through 1.51.0 as affected and records a change to unaffected status at 1.51.1.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE vulnerability record with Patchstack advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agentimus - AI SEO, llms.txt & MCP for AI Agents WordPress plugin through 1.51.0; fixed at 1.51.1; NVD CVSS 8.1 HIGH; CWE-862
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A public CMS plugin that exposes MCP/AI-agent functionality expands tool authority to web roles; subscriber-level broken access control is a direct least-privilege risk.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Broad WordPress plugin cataloging belongs upstream; ai-security-wiki should keep the MCP plugin role-boundary and authorization failure.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE metadata; Patchstack detail may need ingest-time review for exact endpoint and privilege prerequisites.

qualifying_findings.title: MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress has missing authorization
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-85306 describes missing authorization in the MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress plugin. The record marks versions through 1.6.5 as affected and 1.6.6 as unaffected.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE vulnerability record with Patchstack advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress through 1.6.5; fixed at 1.6.6; NVD CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM; CWE-862
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The connector is explicitly an AI MCP bridge for WordPress, so missing authorization can expose delegated tool or content actions beyond intended CMS roles.
named_entities: MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Broad plugin and WordPress ecosystem coverage belongs upstream; ai-security-wiki should keep the MCP connector authorization-control implication.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE metadata; plugin endpoint details should be confirmed from Patchstack during ingest if available.

qualifying_findings.title: Agent-S model-generated GUI action workflow can be driven into denial of service
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-84887 reports a remotely exploitable denial-of-service issue in simular-ai Agent-S through 0.3.2. The affected component is grounding.py in the model-generated GUI action execution workflow; the exploit is public and vendor response was not recorded in the CVE data.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE vulnerability record with VulDB and public proof-of-concept references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: simular-ai Agent-S 0.3.0, 0.3.1, and 0.3.2; NVD CVSS 4.3 MEDIUM; CWE-404
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: GUI action agents need bounded model-generated action parameters and resource controls; this record ties model-generated desktop/browser action execution to availability risk.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: General Agent-S framework coverage belongs in ai-wiki or ai-dev-wiki depending on existing ownership; ai-security-wiki should keep the model-generated GUI action and DoS control boundary.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence from NVD and CVE metadata; fixed-version status is not identified and needs ingest-time reconciliation.

qualifying_findings.title: openbrowser browser-agent message construction can consume resources
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-84833 reports a remotely triggerable resource-consumption vulnerability in ntegrals openbrowser, affecting packages/core/src/agent/agent.ts in the Browser Agent Message Construction component. The CVE notes a rolling-release model with no clean affected or updated release boundary and public exploit availability.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD keyword query evidence and CVE vulnerability record with VulDB and public proof-of-concept references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ntegrals openbrowser commit 067fc45d649baa961750da8e2f4a75d87c5c75c8; no fixed release identified
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser agents process untrusted web and task context into action-planning messages; message budget failures can become denial-of-service controls failures in autonomous browsing workflows.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: General openbrowser framework coverage belongs upstream; ai-security-wiki should keep the browser-agent message-budget and availability-control issue.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence; NVD per-CVE fetch hit HTTP 429 later in the run, so the artifact records the earlier NVD query timestamp plus direct CVE JSON.
